# Final memory budget reporting and delivery verification

The allocation policy is the same one exercised by the full native battery in [[sources/runs/2026/09/2026-09-18-memory-budget-native-verification]]. That battery retains its pre-existing image follow-up reuse failure. The final changes calculate and display the actual residual planning budget, describe the cache as capacity at load, expose additive JSON metadata and correct CLI help wording. They do not change allocations, kernels or generation.

The reporting build passes all 319 memory-override cases, all 90 planner checks, 130 context CLI assertions, 964,237 pure production-source policy assertions, and 48 T0 groups with 28,623 assertions. The new memory-budget group contains 85 assertions, including small-budget headroom and raw-pool reporting. No model is loaded by these checks.

The delivery build differs from that reporting build only in two CLI help wording corrections. An exact archived-source comparison verifies this. The delivery build repeats the 48 T0 groups and 130 context CLI assertions and passes direct help, 48 GB planning and minimum-cache headroom checks. The evidence below binds each result to its own binary; the full native suite was not rerun for those presentation-only changes.

Commands (from the repository root):

```sh
python3 Tools/memory_override_gate.py --binary .build/memory-reviewed/slotstream --out .build/memory-reviewed-overrides.json
SLOTSTREAM_TEST_BINARY=.build/memory-reviewed/slotstream Tools/planner_gates.sh
python3 Tools/context_proxy.py --out .build/memory-reviewed-context-policy
.build/memory-reviewed/slotstream-checks --tier t0
python3 Tools/context_gates.py --binary .build/memory-reviewed/slotstream --report .build/memory-reviewed-context-cli.json
.build/memory-delivery/slotstream-checks --tier t0
python3 Tools/context_gates.py --binary .build/memory-delivery/slotstream --report .build/memory-delivery-context-cli.json
```

The direct UX commands and their exact output are embedded below. All 64 GB / 48 GB cases are planner simulations, not a real 48 GB model allocation. No speed claim or new hardware qualification is made.

memory, and whether it stayed inside the plan\n\nUSAGE: slotstream context-check <options>\n\nOPTIONS:\n  --model <model>         Model name or directory (default\n                          qwen3.8-flash-next:4bit; a name resolves to the dev\n                          checkout's models/ or ~/.slotstream/models) (default:\n                          qwen3.8-flash-next:4bit)\n  --memory-gb <memory-gb> Total memory target for the whole process, in GB.\n        The easiest knob: how much of this Mac slotstream may use. The expert\n        cache gets what remains after the conservatively charged\n        resident/runtime/context footprint and a nominal 1 GB margin. Run\n        `slotstream doctor --memory-gb N` for the exact cache size. This is a\n        budget, not an instruction to fill RAM: context and temporary workspace\n        use memory as needed. Auto will not trade away cache above the measured\n        decode range for more context; --max-context N chooses that tradeoff\n        explicitly. Default: auto -- a model-specific target based on measured\n        tradeoffs, bounded by 70% of RAM, the Metal working set minus 2 GB, and\n        live availability. The chosen plan is announced at startup. An explicit\n        target pins the cache and disables auto resizing. --experts-per-layer /\n        --pool-gb take precedence.\n  --experts-per-layer <experts-per-layer>\n                          Expert cache size, in experts per layer (1...512).\n        The precise memory<->speed knob. Each of the 48 layers has 512 experts\n        of 2.76 MB; the cache holds N x 48 of them, so pool = N x 0.133 GB\n        (e.g. 226/layer = 30 GB, 181/layer = 24 GB, 30/layer = 4 GB) plus the\n        fixed runtime/context footprint. The pool itself is one GLOBAL cache\n        shared across layers -- N is the intuitive unit, not a per-layer quota:\n        hot layers borrow slots from cold ones. Takes precedence over\n        --memory-gb/--pool-gb. Default: auto (see `slotstream doctor`).\n  --pool-gb <pool-gb>     Raw expert-pool size in GB (1 GB \u2248 7.5\n                          experts/layer). Beats --memory-gb; loses to\n                          --experts-per-layer.\n  --max-ram-percent <max-ram-percent>\n                          Auto only: the largest share of this Mac's RAM auto\n                          may target (default 70).\n        Lower it to keep more of the machine for your other apps; auto still\n        sizes down on its own when they are actually holding memory. It cannot\n        raise the model's default ceiling, which reflects measured tradeoffs on\n        tested hardware. Use --memory-gb for an explicit target beyond that\n        ceiling. Ignored when an explicit memory knob is given.\n  --mtp <mtp>             Speculative decode with the MTP draft head: auto | on\n                          | off (default auto). (default: auto)\n        The model's own next-next-token head drafts 2 tokens by default and the\n        main model verifies them in one batched pass. SLOTSTREAM_DRAFT_DEPTH\n        overrides the depth (1...16). Costs a fixed 1.6 GB of memory; auto\n        enables it only when the expert cache still reaches ~120 experts/layer\n        after paying, which is where the multiplier beats spending the same RAM\n        on cache.
